cards.title: Snap bus trails to the streets (OSRM)
cards.brief:
The 10-minute bus trail was a straight line between GPS pings. It now uses the same public OSRM driving router as Calculate route.

What’s live

  • One OSRM request per in-view bus (trail waypoints, max 20). Queued two at a time so we do not hammer the public router.
  • Straight line first, then it snaps when OSRM answers. Result is cached until the trail changes.
  • Fade still runs along the snapped path. Trail clicks do not add waypoints.

Hard-refresh /app/. Wiki: Live buses.

cards.title: Show / hide phones on the map, remembered
cards.brief:
Noah added a Show phones / Hide phones control, same pattern as buses. Preference is stored in localStorage (hackathon-map-phones) so it survives a refresh.

f35b560. Hard-refresh /app/.

cards.title: 10-minute fading trail behind each bus
cards.brief:
Each live bus keeps where it has been for the last 10 minutes. The trail fades to invisible at 10 minutes.

What’s live

  • API stores trails on Firestore BusCache/newcastle — [lng, lat, unix] per vehicle, pruned at 10 minutes.
  • History only grows while a tab is looking (same lazy fetch as card 45). Idle: no new points.
  • Map draws the trail in the bus’s colour, older segments more transparent. Clicks pass through.

API 0.1.8. Hard-refresh /app/. Wiki: Live buses.

cards.title: Cache live buses in Firestore; map reads our API
cards.brief:
Every map tab was calling bustimes.org every 15s. That does not scale, and it hammers someone else’s feed.

What’s live

  • Map GET /v1/buses only while Show buses is on. Hidden tab and Off: no request.
  • API serves Firestore BusCache/newcastle if it is younger than 15s. Otherwise it fetches bustimes.org once, slims the payload, writes the snapshot.
  • Unlimited looking tabs, one upstream refresh. Nobody looking: no refresh.
  • Phone GPS and map GETs stay open. Bustimes.org is never called from the browser.

API 0.1.7. Wiki: Live buses.

cards.title: API user accounts / OAuth2 token
cards.brief:
Noah shipped register, login, and GET /users/me on API 0.1.6 (830036a). Live /health is now 0.1.7 (buses cache on top). No further Noah commits after this card.

What’s live

  • API: POST /register, POST /login (JSON), POST /token (OAuth2 form), GET /users/me (bearer). Users persist in Firestore, Datastore fallback, process cache.
  • Site 625b5dc: /account.html — create account, log in, Fetch me. Token in sessionStorage.
  • Phone GPS, map GETs, and /v1/buses stay open. Only /users/me requires a token.
  • Set JWT_SECRET_KEY on Cloud Run so tokens survive a new revision.

Wiki: API.

cards.title: Buses: viewport, dots then chips, no waypoint steal
cards.brief:
First buses toggle (39) drew every live vehicle in 30 miles as a rotated line chip — about 300 labels, unreadable at city zoom, and a click dropped a waypoint.

What’s live

  • Draw only what is in the current view. Pan/zoom repaints the last fetch; no extra request.
  • Drawn at every zoom. Below 14: coloured dots. Zoom 14+: upright line-number chips, heading pip, operator colour.
  • Pings older than 10 minutes stay hidden. Status shows newest ping age so the feed is visibly moving.
  • Bus click opens a popup and does not add a waypoint.

Hard-refresh /app/. Demo /app/?buses=1 or &zoom=14. Wiki: Live buses.

cards.title: Show buses actually fetches; ghost buttons hover
cards.brief:
Live map: Show buses stayed on “Off — no data fetched” because the first fetch was aborted by stopBusPoll(). Clear and Show buses are btn-ghost and had no hover or pointer, so they felt dead.

What’s live

  • First fetch runs, then the 15s poll. Sidebar sits above the map so clicks land.
  • Ghost buttons hover (amber wash) and use cursor: pointer.

f596040. Hard-refresh /app/ if the old JS is cached.

cards.title: Tracker POSTs every minute; pin on Newcastle
cards.brief:
Emulator sat still and the map age froze. The app now POSTs every minute even if lat/lng are unchanged. recorded_at is last communication, which is the map timestamp.

This AVD ignores console geo fix and caches Google HQ. High-accuracy GPS plus a remap of that HQ default puts the debug pin on Grey’s Monument. A real GPS fix is used as-is.

Commits: cc59adc heartbeat, 38690d0 communication time, 0fb80ce Newcastle.

57a1d44. Cloud Run still execs app/main.py (uvicorn.run(app) stays at the bottom).

Noah, 11 September 2026, 76d3a41.

cards.title: Show history as a route on the map

What’s live

  • API GET /v1/locations?device_id= reads Firestore, Datastore fallback, source in the JSON.

Noah, 11 September 2026.

cards.title: Android app: tracking toggle, GPS to the API
cards.brief:
One switch on hackathon-android: tracking on or off. While on, the phone reads GPS and POSTs to the API. Device id is Android ID (serial/IMEI are locked on modern Android).

Done when

  • A debug APK installs on a phone or emulator.
  • Toggle on starts a foreground location service; toggle off stops it.
  • The phone POSTs /v1/locations with device id, lat, lng.

What’s live (11 September 2026)

  • Pixel 6a emulator: POST HTTP 200 stored=datastore, device android-c55e59830b71ba38.
  • API stores the ping (card 33). Map draws it (card 34). The three-slice path is working.
  • Log tag TynesideTracker. POSTs every minute (heartbeat) even if lat/lng are unchanged. recorded_at is last communication.
  • This AVD ignores geo fix; the debug app remaps Google HQ last-known to Grey’s Monument, Newcastle.

A physical phone is card 35.

cards.title: API stores GPS pings in the database
cards.brief:
Live phones need the API to accept POST /v1/locations (device id, lat, lng) and persist last-known position so the map can read it back. Datastore, same as the rest of the API. /health stays cheap if the database is down.

Done when

  • A POST from the Android app writes a device’s last lat/lng.
  • GET /v1/devices returns last-known phones for the map.
  • History can live in a ping kind; last-known is enough for v0.

What’s live (11 September 2026)

  • Cloud Run: emulator POST HTTP 200 stored=datastore. Code VERSION 0.1.5.
  • GET /v1/devices returns last-known phones. History: GET /v1/locations?device_id= (Firestore, Datastore fallback).
  • Kinds: Device (last-known) and LocationPing (history).

Shipped on main so the demo works. Repo: hackathon-api.

Shipped on main so the demo works. Repo: hackathon-site.

cards.title: Noah: API talks to Firestore
cards.brief:
Wire hackathon-api to Firestore (code currently imports Datastore in POST /create_field). The handler should take a real key/value, write it, and read it back. Cloud Run is live; this is persistence, not deploy.

Done when

  • POST /create_field (or a clearer route) stores a field in GCP and returns an id.
  • A GET can read that field back from the live API.
  • /health still works if Firestore is down.
  • The Cloud Run service account has datastore/firestore access.

How

  1. Use the official client (google-cloud-firestore or Datastore — pick one and document it).
  2. Do not import the client at module top if that can crash Cloud Run when credentials are missing — lazy import or catch and return 503.
  3. Add a GET so Alpine can prove the round-trip (extend api-test.html or a new island).
